tool_input.description: Inspect exp 13 metrics and run dirs

result:
I've written the design for experiment 14 to `runs/pending_experiment.json` and checked that the file parses. The harness implements, trains and scores it next.

**Starting point (exp 13, the current best):** 0.435 on the held-out 2024 photograph: 60.25% usable, 3.75% false fix, 36% abstain. When the model does answer, it is right about 94% of the time. So almost all of what's left to win is in the abstentions.

**Why I think it abstains:** the training log of exp 13 shows the model still describes the same place differently in each of its three training photographs. Its pick of map tile for a place matches across all three only about 74% of the time, and roughly a quarter of the place description's spread comes from which survey the picture was taken from. On a fourth photograph, that pushes places off their tiles, and the two-model confidence gate turns that into an abstention.

**The change:** in the early layers of the pretrained network, the per-channel averages and spreads act like a photograph's "filter": season, shadows, how each survey was processed. During training, half the time each view gets its filter blended with another view's from the same batch, which is usually from a different survey. Street and roof layout is left untouched. This is a published technique (MixStyle, ICLR 2021), and no earlier experiment in any era has tried it. Exp 6 tried to mix surveys at the pixel level, which smeared the content and was reverted; this mixes only the style.

**What stays fixed:** it acts only in training, so the exported model is the same graph as exp 13 and the size and latency gates don't change. Everything else stays as in exp 13. Nothing under `model/` touches the 2024 photograph.

**Prediction:** a score of about 0.33–0.38, with usable rising to 65–70% and false fixes staying at or below 4%. The survey-dependence measures in the training log should improve. If those measures improve but usable on 2024 doesn't, then style in the early layers was not what separates 2024 from the training photographs, and the next experiment should look at the deeper layers or the training targets instead.
